detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

Extends verl's delta weight sync (`delta_sharded` checkpoint engine, #6974 / #7227, roadmap #7060) to **Ascend NPU** hosts via an **HCCL transport**, so NPU training runs can skip full-weight resyncs between trainer and rollout the same way CUDA hosts already do. Design discussion: RFC #7787.

Highlights:

- **Zero new config for NPU users** — the same `backend=delta_sharded` auto-selects the HCCL delta engine on NPU (the NCCL delta module requires `cupy` and fails to import there) and the NCCL engine on CUDA; the vLLM weight-transfer backend likewise defaults to `verl_delta_hccl` on NPU, `verl_delta_ipc` elsewhere.
- **One pipeline, two transports** — the seed/steady state machine, bucketing and flush manifests are extracted into a transport-agnostic `DeltaSyncMixin` shared by the NCCL and HCCL engines; the CUDA path is refactored but behaviorally unchanged (guarded by the existing GPU suites).
- **Direct broadcast into the vLLM workers** — NPU has no CUDA IPC, so the trainer's rank 0 broadcasts each flush into a persistent PyHccl broadcast group whose members are the vLLM worker processes themselves: one zmq manifest subscription plus two broadcasts per flush, no IPC-handle negotiation.

**Scope and limitations (first revision):** vLLM rollout only, BF16 non-quantized **dense** models, TP ∈ {1, 2}, `data_parallel_size=1`, `pipeline_parallel_size=1`, `verify_every=0`; `rebuild_group=True` and the SGLang receiver raise `NotImplementedError` (SGLang rides the CUDA IPC path; the HCCL group is persistent). **MoE models are rejected at startup with an explicit error** — NPU has no Triton (MoE delta loads are Triton-only on CUDA today), and expert-parallel sharding needs its own bookkeeping on the trainer and rollout sides. MoE support is the immediate follow-up to this PR (roadmap: *NPU MoE delta updates*), with DP/PP generalization after that. Worker crash/restart mid-session is likewise follow-up.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: [delta-sync / HCCL / NPU query](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+delta+sync+hccl+npu) — all existing delta-sync work is NCCL/CUDA-only; the closest open PRs (#7777, #7778) improve the CUDA-side gather with no overlap (a small rebase is expected if they land first); vllm-ascend#13682 uses runtime coordinates in a different repo, not consumable here; no verl PR other than our RFC #7787 asks for NPU/HCCL delta sync. Refreshed on 2026-10-27 against main `7e14b6be`.
- [x] Title follows `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` — `[ckpt, rollout, vllm] feat: support delta weight sync on Ascend NPU (HCCL transport)` (also checked by the CI title workflow).

### Test

Covered by existing CI workflows (no new workflow):

| suite | what it proves | CI |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/checkpoint_engine/test_correctness_on_npu.py` (extended) | end-to-end `DeltaHCCLCheckpointEngine` sync over the real HCCL wire — seed / perturbed-steady / zero-change rounds with bit-exact per-parameter checks; bucket chunking at 3072 MB / 128 MB, TP ∈ {1, 2} | `npu_unit_tests.yml` |
| `test_delta_decode_on_cpu.py`, `test_delta_checksum_on_cpu.py` (new) | device-agnostic wire decode and order-sensitive 64-bit checksum | `cpu_unit_tests.yml` (`tests/**/test_*_on_cpu.py` pattern) |
| `test_delta_wire_fail_loud_on_cpu.py` (new) | corruption / protocol-violation fail-loud paths | `vllm.yml` (added to its CPU unit-test list) |
| `test_correctness_on_gpu.py`, `tests/special_distributed/test_sharded_delta_gather.py` (existing) | the NCCL/CUDA path is behaviorally unchanged by the `DeltaSyncMixin` refactor | existing GPU suites |

Manual validation on an NPU cluster (4 training + 2 inference nodes, 32 trainers × 16 rollout workers, Qwen3.5-9B dense BF16):

```shell
# E2E correctness — two combined cases of the 2x2 (bucket x tp) matrix:
#   (3072 MB, tp=1) large-bucket baseline + (128 MB, tp=2) small-bucket chunking stress
pytest "tests/checkpoint_engine/test_correctness_on_npu.py::test_delta_hccl_checkpoint_engine" -v \
  -k "(bucket_size_mb3072 and tensor_parallel_size1) or (bucket_size_mb128 and tensor_parallel_size2)"
```

**E2E results** — both selected cases PASSED on the 4+2 cluster (Qwen3.5-9B): `(3072 MB, tp=1)` in 663 s and `(128 MB, tp=2)` in 645 s. Each case validates three rounds bit-exactly: the seed full sync (`changed_ratio=1.0`), a deterministic sparse perturbation (`0.3 < changed_ratio < 0.7`), and a zero-change steady round (terminal-only session, zero flushes, weights untouched). The cluster model is a VLM, so `check_weights` aligns the trainer's `model.`-prefixed HF names with the `AutoModel` backbone reference — plain CausalLM checkpoints (the CI default) work the same way. The wire checksum was strengthened during review (from an 8-bit byte fold to the order-sensitive 64-bit fold — see the review thread); the runs above predate that change, and the strengthened fold is pinned by the CPU checksum unit tests and re-exercised end-to-end by the CI NPU suites.

**Real-training E2E** — the same cluster ran a verl `FullyAsyncPolicy` training job end-to-end with `backend=delta_sharded` (Qwen3.5-9B dense BF16, 2 steps): Megatron trainer (TP=4, DP=8 = 32 NPUs) + vLLM rollout (16 NPUs, TP=2), default 2048 MB flush buckets. 2/2 steps completed, three weight syncs through the HCCL delta path (seed + two steady rounds — measurements below), training metrics sane. This exercises the production receiver geometry — the vLLM worker processes themselves join the trainer's PyHccl broadcast group — and a Megatron-side shard export feeding the new engine with no trainer-side changes; the mock-receiver test above covers neither.

**Measurements** (from that run; deltas are applied inside the vLLM workers through the real weight-update path):

| sync round | changed_ratio | wire payload | wire time | param_sync wall | reduction vs seed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v=0 seed (full sync) | 100 % | 17.5 GB | 23.2 s | 37.2 s | 1.0x (baseline) |
| v=1 delta | 2.27 % | 1222.5 MB | 6.5 s | 22.3 s | 14.3x |
| v=2 delta | 1.26 % | 680.4 MB | 4.6 s | 14.4 s | 25.7x |

Delta payloads shrink as training converges (2.27 % → 1.26 % of elements changed); at step 2 the whole weight sync (22.3 s) is ~5.5 % of the 404 s training step. The production default (2048 MB) sits in the same large-bucket regime as the 3072 MB test case — both exceed the largest single weight, so only the 128 MB case exercises intra-weight chunking.

Environment: Ascend 910B3 (CANN 9.1.0), vLLM 0.23.0 + vllm-ascend 0.23; the PR targets current vLLM main APIs, so the run went through a test-only compatibility shim (kept out of the PR).

### API and Usage Example

No new config surface — NPU reuses the CUDA vLLM-path configuration verbatim; the platform decides the transport:

```bash
# identical config on NPU and CUDA hosts
actor_rollout_ref.rollout.checkpoint_engine.backend=delta_sharded
# optional, same as on CUDA:
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.checkpoint_engine.engine_kwargs.delta_sharded.encoding=indices
```

Per-sync observability returned by `CheckpointEngineManager.update_weights`: `checkpoint_engine/changed_ratio`, `changed_elems`, `payload_mbytes`, `flushes`, `elapsed_seconds`; the seed round additionally logs its one-off full-model cost.

### Design & Code Changes

The delta-sync pipeline is transport-agnostic at its core — the seed/steady state machine, bucketing and manifest publishing do not care how bytes reach the receiver. This PR extracts that core into `DeltaSyncMixin` (`verl/checkpoint_engine/delta_sync/pipeline.py`), and each transport implements only the wire via four hooks:

| hook | contract |
|---|---|
| `_wire_device` | device the flush tensors are assembled and broadcast from (`cuda` / `npu`) |
| `_ensure_wire` | lazy transport init, called before each flush's manifest is published |
| `_broadcast_flush` | put one flush's raw uint8 buffers on the wire — `(pos_u8, val_u8)`, positions absent for values-only flushes (the seed) |
| `_release_after_round` | return transport staging memory after each round |

The `_ensure_wire` ordering is deliberate: receivers subscribe to the zmq manifest before joining the broadcast group, so *group ready ⇒ subscribed*, and publishing the manifest after this hook stays lossless despite zmq PUB's drop-before-subscribe semantics.

```
trainer side                                    rollout side (vLLM worker process)
─────────────                                   ─────────────────────────────────
FSDP shard export (unchanged, #7227 contract)
        │
DeltaSyncMixin (delta_sync/pipeline.py)   ←  shared state machine, bucketing,
        │                                      zmq manifest publishing
        ├── NCCL engine (delta_checkpoint_engine.py) → CUDA IPC → vLLM / SGLang
        └── HCCL engine (delta_hccl_checkpoint_engine.py)
                │ trainer rank 0                     VerlDeltaHCCLWeightTransferEngine
                │  PyHccl broadcast group ─────────▶ (delta_weight_transfer.py +
                │  (members = the vLLM workers)        delta_sync/hccl_receiver.py)
```

20 files, +2375/−629, as six independently reviewable commits (design rationale and the open questions — receiver geometry, backend naming, checksum negotiation, relationship to vllm-ascend#13682 — are discussed in RFC #7787):

1. `[ckpt] refactor: extract transport-agnostic delta sync pipeline from the NCCL engine` — the state machine, bucketing and zmq manifest publishing move into `delta_sync/pipeline.py` as `DeltaSyncMixin`; `delta_checkpoint_engine.py` keeps only the NCCL transport, GPU behavior unchanged.
2. `[ckpt, rollout] refactor: extract device-agnostic DeltaFlush decode into delta_sync.decode` — `decode_delta_wire` validates one received flush (spec, encoding, slice bounds, checksum) into plain `DeltaPatch` entries.
3. `[ckpt] feat: add HCCL delta weight sync engine for Ascend NPU` — `DeltaHCCLCheckpointEngine` = `DeltaSyncMixin` on top of the dense HCCL engine (#4885), registered under the same `delta_sharded` name with import success arbitrating per platform; adds `delta_sync/hccl_receiver.py`; the wire checksum switches from `torch.hash_tensor` (no NPU kernel) to a device-side order-sensitive 64-bit fold (position-mixed words, bounded chunks).
4. `[rollout, vllm] feat: add verl_delta_hccl weight-transfer backend for NPU rollouts` — `VerlDeltaHCCLWeightTransferEngine` joins the trainer's PyHccl broadcast group inside the vLLM worker process (SUB + communicator created once, reused across sessions); the rollout adapter only drives worker-lifecycle RPCs with per-worker group ranks.
5. `[ckpt, rollout] test` — the suites listed under *Test*.
6. `[ckpt, rollout] doc` — `docs/advance/delta_weight_sync.md` gains the *Ascend NPU (HCCL transport)* section; the roadmap gains *NPU MoE delta updates*.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and `AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): the repo-local sanity hooks, `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the branch; `mypy` / `autogen-trainer-cfg` need a full-deps environment and run via CI (the workflow runs are awaiting first-time-contributor approval).
- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs): `docs/advance/delta_weight_sync.md` gains the *Ascend NPU (HCCL transport)* section.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows): the E2E extends `tests/checkpoint_engine/test_correctness_on_npu.py` (run by `npu_unit_tests.yml`); the CPU units ride `cpu_unit_tests.yml`'s `*_on_cpu.py` pattern and `vllm.yml`'s CPU list.
- [x] AI assistance disclosed per `AGENTS.md` (see the attribution note below); the human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests attached under *Test*.
- [x] Once this PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ) (if not accessible, the [Feishu group (飞书群)](https://applink.larkoffice.com/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=772jd4f1-cd91-441e-a820-498c6614126a) is the documented alternative). A ci-request message was sent via the Feishu group on 2026-10-19 (no Slack access); CI workflows are awaiting maintainer approval.
- [x] `recipe` submodule — N/A (does not touch `recipe/`).

---

**AI assistance disclosure** (per `AGENTS.md`): the code, tests and documentation in this PR were developed with AI assistance (see the `Co-authored-by:` trailers on the commits). The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and ran the tests whose results are attached under *Test*. This PR does not duplicate any open PR (see *Checklist Before Starting*).

+On Ascend NPU the vLLM path rides the trainer's HCCL broadcast group instead
+of CUDA IPC — see [Ascend NPU (HCCL transport)](#ascend-npu-hccl-transport)
+below.
+
+## Ascend NPU (HCCL transport)
+
+The same ``delta_sharded`` backend ships an HCCL transport for Ascend NPU
+hosts. The checkpoint engine, wire schema, seed/steady state machine and flush
+manifests are shared with the NCCL variant — only the transport and the
+rollout-side receiver differ. No extra configuration: on NPU hosts the
+registry auto-selects the HCCL engine for the ``delta_sharded`` name (the NCCL
+delta module fails to import there — it needs cupy), and on CUDA hosts the
+NCCL engine keeps the name. Likewise the vLLM weight-transfer backend defaults
+to ``verl_delta_hccl`` on NPU and ``verl_delta_ipc`` elsewhere, so the same
+``backend=delta_sharded`` config drives both platforms.
+
+### How the transport differs
+
+- **Direct broadcast into the vLLM workers**: CUDA IPC
+  does not exist on NPU, so flushes are not forwarded through the rollout
+  adapter. Instead the trainer's rank 0 broadcasts each flush (positions +
+  values) into a **PyHccl broadcast group whose members are the vLLM worker
+  processes themselves** — one manifest subscription plus two broadcasts per
+  flush, no payload forwarding hop, no IPC handle negotiation. Group ranks:
+  trainer rank 0 at slot 0, rollout workers 1..N (replica-major /
+  tp-minor).
+- **Manifests over zmq PUB/SUB**: every flush is preceded by a manifest
+  published on a zmq PUB socket (topic ``bucket_metadata``). Receivers connect
+  their SUB *before* joining the broadcast group and raise a per-rank
+  ``delta_wire_ready`` flag in the group's TCPStore after joining; the trainer
+  polls those flags before publishing the first manifest. The flags are
+  required because ``zmq.Socket.connect()`` is asynchronous — a "connected"
+  SUB can still miss the first published manifest (a zmq PUB socket drops
+  messages published before any subscriber connected), and zmq offers no
+  subscription acknowledgment — the process-level wire-ready flag is the only
+  ordering signal available.
+- **Persistent group**: HCCL group setup is expensive, so the communicator is
+  built once at the first sync and kept across rounds (the vLLM worker
+  engines cache theirs too). ``rebuild_group=True`` raises
+  ``NotImplementedError``. A failed session destroys the communicator from
+  whichever side failed, so the whole group fails fast instead of hanging in
+  the next collective — a full job restart is required.
+- **Device-neutral checksum**: the per-flush wire checksum is a device-side
+  order-sensitive 64-bit fold rather than ``torch.hash_tensor`` (whose kernels
+  are CPU/CUDA only), so sender and receiver agree on NPU as well.
+- **Rollout adapter**: on NPU the flush stream the vLLM rollout adapter sees
+  is a single ``__delta_rendezvous__`` control item (the zmq + group
+  endpoints); the adapter only drives the worker engines' weight-transfer
+  lifecycle RPCs, and the per-worker update entries carry each worker's group
+  rank. The update RPC returns only after the session's last flush is
+  applied, so no extra synchronization is needed.
+
+### Requirements and scope
+
+- An Ascend NPU host with CANN + ``torch_npu``, and vllm-ascend providing
+  vLLM's engine-owned weight-transfer and checkpoint patch APIs.
+- vLLM rollout only (the SGLang receiver rides the CUDA IPC path). BF16,
+  non-quantized, no speculative decoding, ``data_parallel_size=1``,
+  ``pipeline_parallel_size=1``, ``verify_every=0`` — the same constraints as
+  the CUDA vLLM path — plus ``tensor_parallel_size`` ∈ {1, 2} in this first
+  revision.
+- **MoE models are not supported on NPU yet** (NPU has no Triton; the
+  vllm-ascend MoE kernel path is in development and will land in a follow-up
+  PR) — startup raises with a pointer to dense models.
+- Trainer side unchanged: the same shard export contract (``Shard(0)``
+  DTensor parameters from FSDP2/FSDP1/TorchTitan) feeds the delta pipeline.
+
+### Observability
+
+``CheckpointEngineManager.update_weights`` returns per-sync metrics
+(``checkpoint_engine/changed_ratio``, ``changed_elems``, ``payload_mbytes``,
+``flushes`` and ``elapsed_seconds``). The seed round additionally logs a
+warning with its one-off full-model cost (the number to check when sizing a
+run), and every steady round logs its elapsed time, changed ratio and wire
+size at info level — visible with ``VERL_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO`` (the worker
+default log level is WARN).
+
+### Testing on an NPU host
+
+```shell
+# end-to-end correctness: 2 trainer x 6 rollout workers over the real HCCL
+# wire (mock apply), seed + sparse-steady + zero-change rounds, bucket
+# chunking (3072MB and 128MB buckets), received weights compared exactly
+pytest tests/checkpoint_engine/test_correctness_on_npu.py -k delta_hccl -v
+```
+
+The decode, checksum and wire units are device-agnostic and run anywhere
+(the wire units skip where vLLM is not installed):
+
+```shell
+pytest tests/checkpoint_engine/test_delta_decode_on_cpu.py \
+       tests/checkpoint_engine/test_delta_checksum_on_cpu.py \
+       tests/checkpoint_engine/test_delta_wire_fail_loud_on_cpu.py -v
+```
+
 ## Roadmap
 
 Planned extensions, in design order:
@@ -220,3 +316,5 @@ Planned extensions, in design order:
   TP column splits are already expressible as a ``BlockPlacement`` dim-1 offset (see #7060).
 - **Quantized rollout (fp8 etc.)**: diff the quantized bytes (quantize-then-diff) so a low-precision
   rollout engine can consume deltas without a bf16 intermediate.
+- **NPU MoE delta updates**: the vllm-ascend kernel path for MoE delta loads (Triton-only on CUDA
+  today), which lifts the NPU dense-model restriction of the HCCL transport.

+class TrainingWorkerDeltaTest(TrainingWorkerTest):
+    """Trainer-side test worker with the engine-driven delta dispatch."""
+
+    @register(dispatch_mode=Dispatch.ONE_TO_ALL, blocking=False)
+    async def update_weights(self, global_steps: int = None, mode: str = "auto"):
+        if mode == "delta_sharded":
+            # parity with engine_workers.py: the delta engine owns the seed/
+            # steady state machine and drives the training engine itself.
+            metrics = await self.checkpoint_engine.send_weights(self.engine, global_steps=global_steps)
+            return metrics or {}
+        return await super().update_weights(global_steps=global_steps, mode=mode)
+
+    @register(dispatch_mode=Dispatch.ONE_TO_ALL)
+    def perturb_positive_half(self):
+        """Deterministic sparse perturbation: every positive element := 2.0.
+
+        The predicate is element-wise (value-based) and the assigned constant
+        is exactly representable in bf16, so applying it independently on every
+        rank's FSDP shard equals applying it once on the full model -- the
+        rollout-side reference computes the identical result from the base
+        weights, and the positive set is invariant across perturbation rounds.
+        """
+        for _, param in self.engine.module.named_parameters():
+            if not param.is_floating_point():
+                continue
+            local = param.to_local() if hasattr(param, "to_local") else param
+            with torch.no_grad():
+                local[local > 0] = 2.0
+
+
+class DeltaHCCLMockServerAdapter(BaseRollout):
+    """Direct-receiver mock standing in for the vLLM worker engines: joins the trainer's PyHccl
+    broadcast group under the rank the single-sender topology assigned to this
+    CheckpointEngineWorker, pulls each session's flushes and applies them to a
+    local weight dict with the wire contract's semantics (checksum verify,
+    dense overwrite / sparse index_copy_). The expected state is the disk model
+    with the same deterministic perturbation applied, compared bit-exactly.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, rollout_config, model_config, check_allclose: bool = True):
+        super().__init__(rollout_config, model_config, device_mesh=None)
+        self.check_allclose = check_allclose
+        self.applied: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
+        self.perturb_rounds = 0
+        self._sub = None
+        self._comm = None
+
+    def _device(self):
+        return torch.device("npu", torch.npu.current_device())
+
+    async def resume(self, tags: list[str]):
+        raise NotImplementedError()
+
+    async def release(self):
+        raise NotImplementedError()
+
+    async def update_weights(self, weights, global_steps=None, wire_format="delta_flush", **kwargs):
+        from verl.workers.rollout.utils import ensure_async_iterator
+
+        assert wire_format == "delta_flush"
+        flushes = ensure_async_iterator(weights)
+        first_named, _ = await anext(flushes)
+        info = _decode_rendezvous(first_named)
+        assert info is not None, "expected the HCCL rendezvous control item"
+        if self._comm is None:
+            # SUB before communicator, and the trainer publishes the first
+            # manifest only after every receiver's wire-ready flag is up, so
+            # subscribing before joining cannot miss any.
+            self._sub = connect_delta_manifest_sub(info["zmq_ip"], info["zmq_port"], info["topic"])
+            self._comm = build_delta_hccl_communicator(
+                info["dist_ip"], info["dist_port"], info["engine_rank"], info["world_size"], self._device()
+            )
+        pump_hccl_delta_session(self._sub, self._comm, self._device(), on_flush=self._apply_flush)
+        async for _ in flushes:
+            pass
+
+    def _apply_flush(self, named: list[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> None:
+        from verl.checkpoint_engine.delta_sync.decode import decode_delta_wire
+
+        encoding, patches = decode_delta_wire(named)
+        for patch in patches:
+            if encoding == "dense":
+                # clone: the broadcast buffers are recycled after this callback
+                self.applied[patch.name] = patch.values.detach().clone().view(patch.shape)
+            else:
+                flat = self.applied[patch.name].view(-1)
+                flat.index_copy_(0, patch.positions.to(torch.int64), patch.values.to(flat.dtype))
+
+    def perturb_reference(self):
+        self.perturb_rounds += 1
+
+    def check_weights(self):
+        if not self.check_allclose:
+            return
+        if not self.applied:
+            raise AssertionError("no delta flushes were applied")
+        local_path = copy_to_local(self.model_config.path)
+        # The trainer sends full-model HF names carrying the "model." wrapper
+        # (e.g. "model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight" on a VLM); AutoModel
+        # returns the backbone state dict without that wrapper, so strip it from
+        # the applied names to align the two. AutoModel also covers VLM
+        # checkpoints (vision tower included), unlike AutoModelForCausalLM.
+        reference = AutoModel.from_pretrained(local_path, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="cpu")
+        expected = reference.state_dict()
+        applied_stripped = {k.removeprefix("model."): v for k, v in self.applied.items()}
+        perturbed = self.perturb_rounds > 0
+        for name, base in expected.items():
+            assert name in applied_stripped, f"weight {name} not received (applied has {len(applied_stripped)} weights)"
+            got = applied_stripped[name]
+            if not perturbed:
+                assert torch.equal(got.cpu(), base), f"weight {name} differs from the base model"
+                continue
+            base_pos = base > 0
+            ok = torch.where(base_pos, got.cpu() == 2.0, got.cpu() == base)
+            assert bool(ok.all()), f"weight {name} differs from the perturbed expectation"
+        del reference
+        print("Delta check passed, all weights are bit-exact!")

+    @register(dispatch_mode=Dispatch.ONE_TO_ALL)

+    @register(dispatch_mode=Dispatch.ONE_TO_ALL)

+def _decode_rendezvous(named_tensors) -> dict | None:
+    for name, tensor in named_tensors:

+"""Unit tests for the delta wire checksum (order-sensitive 128-bit dual fold).
+
+Runs on CPU anywhere torch is installed, and on NPU/GPU devices when visible;
+the checksum is a pure function of tensor bytes, so these assertions hold on
+every device.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import verl.checkpoint_engine.delta_sync.encode as encode
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.delta_sync.encode import _wire_digest, checksum
+
+_MASK64 = (1 << 64) - 1
+_MASK128 = (1 << 128) - 1
+_POS_MIX = 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15  # unsigned twin of encode._POS_MIX
+_AVALANCHE_MIX = 0xFF51AFD7ED558CCD  # unsigned twin of encode._AVALANCHE_MIX
+_AVALANCHE_MIX2 = 0xC4CEB9FE1A85EC53  # unsigned twin of encode._AVALANCHE_MIX2
+
+
+def _ref_digest(raw: bytes) -> int:
+    """Pure-python reference for ``_wire_digest`` (little-endian int64 words)."""
+    n8 = len(raw) // 8 * 8
+    fold = 0
+    total = 0
+    for i in range(n8 // 8):
+        w = int.from_bytes(raw[i * 8 : (i + 1) * 8], "little")
+        v = (w + _POS_MIX * (i + 1)) & _MASK64
+        v = ((v ^ (v >> 33)) * _AVALANCHE_MIX) & _MASK64
+        v = ((v ^ (v >> 29)) * _AVALANCHE_MIX2) & _MASK64
+        v = v ^ (v >> 32)
+        fold ^= v
+        total = (total + v) & _MASK64
+    tail = 0
+    for i in range(n8, len(raw)):
+        tail ^= raw[i] << (8 * (i - n8))
+    return (((total + tail) & _MASK64) << 64) | ((fold ^ tail) & _MASK64)
+
+
+def test_empty_arguments_checksum_to_zero():
+    pos = torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    val = torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    assert _wire_digest(pos) == 0
+    assert checksum(pos, val) == 0
+
+
+def test_matches_reference():
+    for n in [1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 31, 64, 100, 4097]:
+        pos = torch.randint(0, 256, (n,), dtype=torch.uint8)
+        val = torch.randn(n + 13).to(torch.bfloat16)
+        assert _wire_digest(pos) == _ref_digest(bytes(pos.tolist()))
+        assert _wire_digest(val) == _ref_digest(bytes(val.view(torch.uint8).tolist()))
+
+
+def test_positions_and_values_combine_deterministically():
+    pos = torch.tensor([1, 2, 3], dtype=torch.uint8)
+    val = torch.tensor([4.0], dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    p = _ref_digest(bytes(pos.tolist()))
+    v = _ref_digest(bytes(val.view(torch.uint8).tolist()))
+    expected = (p ^ (((v << 1) | (v >> 127)) & _MASK128)) & _MASK128
+    assert checksum(pos, val) == expected
+    assert checksum(pos, val) == checksum(pos.clone(), val.clone())
+
+
+def test_int64_sum_folds_wraparound_mod_2_64():
+    # The sum fold relies on torch int64 reduction wrapping mod 2**64 (no
+    # promotion, no overflow error); pin that semantics explicitly.
+    v = torch.full((4,), 1 << 62, dtype=torch.int64)
+    assert int(v.sum()) == 0  # wraps: 4 * 2**62 == 2**64 == 0 mod 2**64
+    big = torch.randint(-(1 << 62), 1 << 62, (4097,), dtype=torch.int64)
+    assert int(big.sum()) & _MASK64 == sum(big.tolist()) & _MASK64
+
+
+def test_single_bit_flip_is_detected():
+    for which in ["pos", "val"]:
+        pos = torch.randint(0, 256, (97,), dtype=torch.uint8)
+        val = torch.randn(33).to(torch.bfloat16)
+        before = checksum(pos, val)
+        if which == "pos":
+            pos = pos.clone()
+            pos[41] ^= 0x01
+        else:
+            val = val.clone()
+            raw = val.view(torch.uint8)
+            raw[5] ^= 0x80
+        assert checksum(pos, val) != before, f"flip in {which} went undetected"
+
+
+def test_reordering_is_detected():
+    raw = torch.arange(64, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    base = _wire_digest(raw)
+    # Swapping two whole words keeps the byte multiset; only the positional
+    # term can catch it.
+    words = raw.view(torch.int64)
+    swapped = words.clone()
+    swapped[0], swapped[5] = words[5].clone(), words[0].clone()
+    assert _wire_digest(swapped.view(torch.uint8)) != base
+    # Swapping two bytes inside one word changes the word value itself.
+    inside = raw.clone()
+    inside[8], inside[9] = raw[9].item(), raw[8].item()
+    assert _wire_digest(inside) != base
+
+
+def test_bit63_word_pair_swap_is_detected():
+    # Deterministic regression: an affine-only position mix (w + K * i) maps
+    # words that differ solely in bit 63 to mixed values that also differ
+    # solely in bit 63 -- adding 2**63 mod 2**64 toggles exactly that bit --
+    # so the XOR fold cancels such swaps. The avalanche step exists to break
+    # this cancellation; keep this case pinned regardless of future mixing.
+    def as_i64(u: int) -> int:
+        return u - (1 << 64) if u >= (1 << 63) else u
+
+    for w1 in (0, 1, 0x123456789ABCDEF, 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF):
+        for i, j in ((0, 1), (0, 5), (1, 2), (3, 7)):
+            words = torch.arange(8, dtype=torch.int64)
+            words[i] = as_i64(w1)
+            words[j] = as_i64(w1 ^ (1 << 63))
+            swapped = words.clone()
+            swapped[i], swapped[j] = words[j].clone(), words[i].clone()
+            assert _wire_digest(swapped.view(torch.uint8)) != _wire_digest(words.view(torch.uint8)), (
+                f"bit-63 pair swap at ({i},{j}) with w1={w1:#x} went undetected"
+            )
+
+
+def test_complementary_word_corruption_is_detected():
+    # Deterministic regression: with an arithmetic (sign-extending) shift in
+    # the avalanche, v ^ (v >> 31) always clears bit 63, so a word w and its
+    # position-twinned complement (-1 - w - 2 * K * p at 1-based position p,
+    # whose mixed values are bitwise complements) collide. The masked logical
+    # shift keeps the avalanche bijective; keep this construction pinned.
+    K = _POS_MIX
+
+    def as_i64(u: int) -> int:
+        return u - (1 << 64) if u >= (1 << 63) else u
+
+    for w in (0, 1, 0x123456789ABCDEF, 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF):
+        for p0 in (0, 1, 3, 7):
+            words = torch.arange(10, dtype=torch.int64)
+            words[p0] = as_i64(w)
+            base = _wire_digest(words.view(torch.uint8))
+            words[p0] = as_i64((-1 - w - 2 * K * (p0 + 1)) & _MASK64)
+            assert _wire_digest(words.view(torch.uint8)) != base, (
+                f"complementary corruption at position {p0} with w={w:#x} went undetected"
+            )
+
+
+def test_topbit_toggle_pair_swaps_are_detected():
+    # Deterministic regression: a single-stage avalanche passes top-bit
+    # toggles through the odd multiply unchanged, so swapping two words whose
+    # position-mixed values differ by exactly the toggle preimage (bit 63:
+    # 0x8000000100000002; bit 62: 0x4000000080000001, which our first odd
+    # constant also passes because it is 1 mod 4) cancels in the XOR fold.
+    # These exact pairs collided before the two-stage avalanche; keep them
+    # pinned regardless of future mixing.
+    def as_i64(u: int) -> int:
+        return u - (1 << 64) if u >= (1 << 63) else u
+
+    pinned = [
+        ((0, 1), 0x8000000080000001, 0xFFFFFFFF7FFFFFFF),
+        ((1, 2), 0x00000000FFFFFFFE, 0x8000000000000000),
+        ((1, 2), 0x0000000100000000, 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFE),
+        ((0, 64), 0x000000007FFFFFFF, 0x4000000000000000),
+        ((3, 7), 0x9E3779B9FF4A7C14, 0xDE3779B97F4A7C15),
+        ((5, 69), 0x0000000000000001, 0x80000000FFFFFFFF),
+    ]
+    for (i, j), w, w2 in pinned:
+        words = [0x1111111111111111] * 80
+        words[i] = w
+        words[j] = w2
+        swapped = list(words)
+        swapped[i], swapped[j] = w2, w
+        base = _wire_digest(torch.tensor([as_i64(x) for x in words], dtype=torch.int64).view(torch.uint8))
+        other = _wire_digest(torch.tensor([as_i64(x) for x in swapped], dtype=torch.int64).view(torch.uint8))
+        assert base != other, f"toggle-family swap at ({i},{j}) {w:#x} <-> {w2:#x} went undetected"
+
+
+def test_two_bit_shift_response_pair_swaps_are_detected():
+    # Deterministic regression: these two-bit difference pairs cancel the XOR
+    # fold alone (they fold into single-bit differences through the avalanche's
+    # xor-shift stages); the sum fold detects them. Collided before the dual
+    # fold; keep pinned regardless of future mixing.
+    def as_i64(u: int) -> int:
+        return u - (1 << 64) if u >= (1 << 63) else u
+
+    pinned = [
+        ((1, 17), 0x3C92AD063D838AB2, 0xBC92AD067D838AB2),
+        ((1, 1000), 0x6E0EC2DA019187AD, 0xEE0EC2DA419187AD),
+        ((3, 17), 0x20AD07FD7C99BCF9, 0xA0AD07FD3C99BCF9),
+        ((3, 33), 0x7F8E25C075D83D25, 0xFF8E25C035D83D25),
+        ((3, 1000), 0x5CA055D303876CD5, 0xDCA055D343876CD5),
+        ((4, 8), 0x7BA1CDBE5ED0B285, 0xFBA1CDBE1ED0B285),
+        ((5, 17), 0x936B87A02E3992A6, 0xD36B87A00E3992A6),
+        ((5, 33), 0x8BFA4052DE8BA43F, 0x9BFA4052D68BA43F),
+    ]
+    for (i, j), w, w2 in pinned:
+        words = [0x1111111111111111] * (j + 10)
+        words[i - 1], words[j - 1] = w, w2
+        base = _wire_digest(torch.tensor([as_i64(x) for x in words], dtype=torch.int64).view(torch.uint8))
+        swapped = list(words)
+        swapped[i - 1], swapped[j - 1] = w2, w
+        other = _wire_digest(torch.tensor([as_i64(x) for x in swapped], dtype=torch.int64).view(torch.uint8))
+        assert base != other, f"two-bit family swap at ({i},{j}) {w:#x} <-> {w2:#x} went undetected"
+
+
+def test_chunked_fold_matches_single_pass(monkeypatch):
+    # The fold accumulates over _FOLD_CHUNK_BYTES chunks; shrinking the chunk
+    # must not change the digest.
+    pos = torch.randint(0, 256, (4097,), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    val = torch.randn(999).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    single = (checksum(pos, val), _wire_digest(pos))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(encode, "_FOLD_CHUNK_BYTES", 32)
+    chunked = (checksum(pos, val), _wire_digest(pos))
+    assert chunked == single
+    assert chunked[1] == _ref_digest(bytes(pos.tolist()))
+
+
+def test_offset_slice_input_is_handled():
+    # A contiguous slice can carry a storage offset the int64 chunk views
+    # reject; those chunks must be re-housed, not crash.
+    raw = torch.arange(17, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    assert _wire_digest(raw[1:17]) == _ref_digest(bytes(raw[1:17].tolist()))
+    vals = torch.randn(40).to(torch.bfloat16)[3:]  # offset 3 elements = 6 bytes
+    assert _wire_digest(vals) == _ref_digest(bytes(vals.view(torch.uint8).tolist()))
+
+
+def test_offset_slice_chunked_matches_reference(monkeypatch):
+    raw = torch.randint(0, 256, (130,), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(encode, "_FOLD_CHUNK_BYTES", 32)
+    for lo in (0, 1, 3, 5):
+        s = raw[lo:]
+        assert _wire_digest(s) == _ref_digest(bytes(s.tolist()))
+
+
+def test_dtype_view_invariance():
+    # same bytes, different dtype interpretation -> same digest
+    raw = torch.randint(0, 256, (64,), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    as_bf16 = raw.view(torch.bfloat16)
+    assert _wire_digest(raw) == _wire_digest(as_bf16)
+    assert _wire_digest(as_bf16.contiguous()) == _wire_digest(as_bf16.reshape(-1, 4).contiguous())
+
+
+def test_input_storage_not_mutated():
+    pos = torch.randint(0, 256, (33,), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    val = torch.randn(17).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    pos_before, val_before = pos.clone(), val.clone()
+    checksum(pos, val)
+    assert torch.equal(pos, pos_before)
+    assert torch.equal(val.view(torch.uint8), val_before.view(torch.uint8))
+
+
+def test_large_tensor_against_reference():
+    pos = torch.randint(0, 256, (1 << 20,), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    val = torch.randn(1 << 18).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    assert _wire_digest(pos) == _ref_digest(bytes(pos.tolist()))
+    assert _wire_digest(val) == _ref_digest(bytes(val.view(torch.uint8).tolist()))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA device not available")
+def test_checksum_agrees_across_cpu_and_cuda():
+    pos = torch.randint(0, 256, (1000,), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    val = torch.randn(777).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    assert checksum(pos, val) == checksum(pos.cuda(), val.cuda())
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":

+def _make_named(dtype=torch.bfloat16) -> list[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]:

+def _sparse_indices_flush(old_named, new_named):
+    """Assemble one indices-encoding flush from a bytewise old/new diff --
+    the same layout the sharded engines' ``_assemble_flush`` produces."""
+    params, idx_pieces, val_pieces = [], [], []
+    pos_off = val_off = 0
+    for (name, old), (_, new) in zip(old_named, new_named, strict=True):
+        fo, fn = old.reshape(-1), new.reshape(-1)
+        changed = (fo.view(torch.uint8).view(fo.numel(), -1) != fn.view(torch.uint8).view(fn.numel(), -1)).any(dim=-1)
+        idx = changed.nonzero(as_tuple=False).view(-1)
+        # Keep zero-length manifest entries, like the real wire: unchanged params
+        # still appear with pos_start == pos_end / val_start == val_end.
+        nnz = int(idx.numel())
+        idx_pieces.append(idx.to(torch.int32))
+        val_pieces.append(fn[idx])
+        params.append(
+            DeltaParam(
+                name=name,
+                dtype=str(new.dtype).replace("torch.", ""),
+                shape=list(new.shape),
+                pos_start=pos_off,
+                pos_end=pos_off + nnz * 4,
+                pos_width=4,
+                val_start=val_off,
+                val_end=val_off + nnz,
+            )
+        )
+        pos_off += nnz * 4
+        val_off += nnz
+    positions = torch.cat(idx_pieces).contiguous().view(torch.uint8)
+    values = torch.cat(val_pieces)
+    return params, positions, values

+def _named_tensors(params, positions, values, encoding="indices"):
+    spec = {

+    }
+    spec_t = torch.frombuffer(bytearray(json.dumps(spec).encode()), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    out = [("__delta_spec__", spec_t), ("__values__", values.clone())]
+    if positions.numel():
+        out.insert(1, ("__positions__", positions.clone()))
+    return out

+"""Fail-loud and wiring unit tests for the delta HCCL receiver path.
+
+The checksum-corruption cases pin the spec's fail-loud requirement: a damaged
+flush must raise, never silently apply. The rendezvous/rank cases pin the
+control contract between the rollout engine and the vLLM worker engines.
+Requires vLLM (the decode path builds CheckpointWeightPatch objects); skips
+cleanly where vLLM is absent.
+"""
+
+import json
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from verl.checkpoint_engine.delta_sync.encode import DeltaParam, checksum
+
+pytest.importorskip("vllm")
+
+
+def _spec_tensor(spec: dict) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.frombuffer(bytearray(json.dumps(spec).encode()), dtype=torch.uint8)
+
+
+def _dense_flush_payload(name: str = "model.layers.0.weight"):
+    values = torch.randn(64).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    spec = {
+        "encoding": "dense",
+        "params": [
+            vars(
+                DeltaParam(
+                    name=name,
+                    dtype="bfloat16",
+                    shape=[8, 8],
+                    pos_start=0,
+                    pos_end=0,
+                    pos_width=4,
+                    val_start=0,
+                    val_end=64,
+                )
+            )
+        ],
+        "checksum": int(checksum(torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.uint8), values)),
+    }
+    return [("__delta_spec__", _spec_tensor(spec)), ("__values__", values)]
+
+
+def test_decode_delta_payload_applies_clean_flush():
+    from verl.workers.rollout.vllm_rollout.delta_weight_transfer import decode_delta_payload
+
+    encoding, patches = decode_delta_payload(_dense_flush_payload())
+    assert encoding == "dense"
+    assert len(patches) == 1 and patches[0].values.numel() == 64
+
+
+def test_decode_delta_payload_fails_loud_on_value_corruption():
+    from verl.workers.rollout.vllm_rollout.delta_weight_transfer import decode_delta_payload
+
+    payload = _dense_flush_payload()
+    raw = payload[1][1].view(torch.uint8)
+    raw[3] ^= 0x40
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="checksum mismatch"):
+        decode_delta_payload(payload)
+
+
+def test_decode_delta_payload_fails_loud_on_spec_corruption():
+    from verl.workers.rollout.vllm_rollout.delta_weight_transfer import decode_delta_payload
+
+    payload = _dense_flush_payload()
+    spec = json.loads(bytes(payload[0][1].numpy().tobytes()).decode())
+    spec["checksum"] = (spec["checksum"] + 1) & ((1 << 128) - 1)
+    payload[0] = ("__delta_spec__", _spec_tensor(spec))
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="checksum mismatch"):
+        decode_delta_payload(payload)
+
+
+def test_decode_delta_rendezvous_roundtrip():
+    from verl.workers.rollout.vllm_rollout.vllm_rollout import _decode_delta_rendezvous
+
+    info = {
+        "mode": "verl_delta_hccl",
+        "zmq_ip": "10.0.0.1",
+        "zmq_port": 1234,
+        "dist_ip": "10.0.0.1",
+        "dist_port": 5678,
+        "topic": "bucket_metadata",
+        "world_size": 7,
+        "engine_rank": 3,
+    }
+    decoded = _decode_delta_rendezvous([("__delta_rendezvous__", _spec_tensor(info))])
+    assert decoded == info
+    assert _decode_delta_rendezvous([("__delta_spec__", torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.uint8))]) is None
+
+
+def test_hccl_group_update_infos_number_replica_major_tp_minor():
+    from verl.workers.rollout.vllm_rollout.vllm_rollout import _hccl_group_update_infos
+
+    assert _hccl_group_update_infos(replica_rank=0, tp_size=1) == [{"group_rank": 1}]
+    assert _hccl_group_update_infos(replica_rank=0, tp_size=2) == [{"group_rank": 1}, {"group_rank": 2}]
+    assert _hccl_group_update_infos(replica_rank=2, tp_size=2) == [{"group_rank": 5}, {"group_rank": 6}]
+    ranks = [u["group_rank"] for u in _hccl_group_update_infos(replica_rank=1, tp_size=3)]
+    assert ranks == [4, 5, 6]
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    pytest.main([__file__])

+"""Delta weight-sync checkpoint engine (HCCL transport) for Ascend NPU rollouts.
+
+Same seed/steady state machine, wire schema and flush manifest as the NCCL
+variant (:mod:`verl.checkpoint_engine.delta_checkpoint_engine`); the transport
+is a ``PyHcclCommunicator`` broadcast group whose consumers are the vLLM worker
+processes themselves (the direct-receiver geometry):
+
+* the trainer-side rank 0 builds its communicator lazily at the first publish
+  and broadcasts each flush's positions+values after the zmq manifest, with an
+  explicit ``torch.npu.synchronize()`` before the buffers go out of scope (no
+  cupy staging: PyHccl enqueues on the current stream, so holding the tensor
+  references across the sync point is sufficient);
+* the rollout-side CheckpointEngineWorkers never join the broadcast group --
+  ``receive_weights`` relays one rendezvous control item (zmq + stateless group
+  endpoints, group geometry) to the rollout adapter, which drives the vLLM
+  worker engines through their weight-transfer lifecycle RPCs;
+* both sides keep the communicator across sync rounds (HCCL group setup is
+  expensive; mirrors the dense HCCL engine's ``rebuild_group=False`` reuse).
+
+The lazy rendezvous is gated by per-rank wire-ready receipts: every receiver
+connects its zmq SUB, joins the group and raises a ``delta_wire_ready/{rank}``
+flag in the group's TCPStore; the trainer polls those flags
+(:func:`verl.checkpoint_engine.delta_sync.hccl_receiver.wait_delta_wire_ready`)
+before publishing the first manifest. Code order alone cannot make the stream
+lossless -- ``zmq.Socket.connect()`` is asynchronous -- while the flags order
+the first publish after every receiver joined, giving each subscription
+(initiated before its join) the whole join duration to reach the PUB socket.

+import json
+import logging
+import os
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+
+import torch

+from verl.utils.device import is_torch_npu_available
+

+    raise ImportError("DeltaHCCLCheckpointEngine is unavailable because the torch.npu module is not available.")

+from .delta_sync.hccl_receiver import wait_delta_wire_ready
+from .delta_sync.pipeline import DeltaSyncMixin
+from .hccl_checkpoint_engine import HCCLCheckpointEngine, MasterMetadata

+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+logger.setLevel(os.getenv("VERL_LOGGING_LEVEL", "WARN"))

+@CheckpointEngineRegistry.register("delta_sharded")

+    """Sparse delta weight sync over HCCL, registered under the same
+    ``delta_sharded`` backend name as the NCCL engine (mirroring how the dense

+"""Device- and backend-agnostic decoding of DeltaFlush payloads.
+
+This is the consumer-free half of the wire decode: it validates one received
+flush (spec JSON, encoding consistency, per-parameter slice bounds, checksum)
+and returns plain per-parameter patches. Backend-specific consumers then
+convert the patches into whatever their loader expects (the vLLM CUDA path
+turns them into ``CheckpointWeightPatch`` via vLLM's checkpoint patch API;
+the NPU HCCL receiver and tests apply them through ``index_copy_`` /
+``model.load_weights``).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from collections.abc import Iterable
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import torch
+
+from .encode import checksum
+
+
+@dataclass
+class DeltaPatch:
+    """One decoded parameter patch in final checkpoint/HF coordinates.
+
+    ``positions`` is an int32 flat-index tensor into the flattened parameter
+    (``None`` for dense/full-coverage flushes); ``values`` holds the
+    corresponding elements in the parameter's dtype.
+    """
+
+    name: str
+    shape: tuple[int, ...]
+    dtype: torch.dtype
+    values: torch.Tensor
+    positions: torch.Tensor | None  # int32 flat positions; None for dense
+
+
+def decode_delta_wire(named_tensors: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> tuple[str, list[DeltaPatch]]:
+    """Validate and decode one DeltaFlush into ``(encoding, [DeltaPatch])``.
+
+    Raises ``ValueError`` on malformed payloads and ``RuntimeError`` on a
+    checksum mismatch (wire corruption).
+    """
+    tensors = dict(named_tensors)
+    try:
+        spec_tensor = tensors["__delta_spec__"]
+        values = tensors["__values__"]
+        spec = json.loads(bytes(spec_tensor.detach().cpu().numpy().tobytes()).decode())
+    except KeyError as exc:
+        raise ValueError(f"DeltaFlush is missing {exc.args[0]}") from exc
+    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
+        raise ValueError("DeltaFlush contains an invalid JSON spec") from exc
+
+    encoding = spec["encoding"]
+    if encoding not in {"dense", "indices"}:
+        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported DeltaFlush encoding: {encoding!r}")
+    positions = tensors.get("__positions__")
+    if positions is None:
+        positions = torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.uint8, device=values.device)
+    if encoding == "dense" and positions.numel():
+        raise ValueError("Dense DeltaFlush must not contain positions")
+    if encoding == "indices" and "__positions__" not in tensors:
+        raise ValueError("Indices DeltaFlush requires __positions__")
+
+    got_checksum = checksum(positions, values)
+    expected_checksum = int(spec["checksum"])
+    if got_checksum != expected_checksum:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Delta checksum mismatch: got {got_checksum}, expected {expected_checksum}")
+
+    patches: list[DeltaPatch] = []
+    for param_spec in spec["params"]:
+        name = param_spec["name"]
+        dtype = getattr(torch, param_spec["dtype"])
+        patch_values = values[param_spec["val_start"] : param_spec["val_end"]]
+        if encoding == "dense":
+            patch_positions = None
+        else:
+            if param_spec["pos_width"] != 4:
+                raise ValueError(f"{name}: indices encoding requires pos_width=4")
+            pos_bytes = positions[param_spec["pos_start"] : param_spec["pos_end"]]
+            if pos_bytes.numel() != patch_values.numel() * 4:
+                raise ValueError(f"{name}: position and value slices have inconsistent lengths")
+            patch_positions = pos_bytes.view(torch.int32)
+
+        patches.append(
+            DeltaPatch(
+                name=name,
+                shape=tuple(param_spec["shape"]),
+                dtype=dtype,
+                values=patch_values,
+                positions=patch_positions,
+            )
+        )
+    return encoding, patches

+    construction is known to achieve both (every single-fold family found so

+    unstructured collisions are ~2**-128. Integer addition is associative, so
+    the sum fold is independent of reduction order and device. Words are

+"""Receiver-side HCCL delta transport: zmq manifest subscription + PyHccl group.
+
+Shared by the vLLM worker engines (the production receivers) and direct
+receivers used in tests. The SUB socket MUST be connected before the
+communicator is built (rendezvous-as-ready-gate). Code order alone cannot make
+the manifest stream lossless -- ``zmq.Socket.connect()`` is asynchronous, so a
+"connected" SUB can still miss the first published manifest -- so every
+receiver raises a per-rank ``delta_wire_ready/{rank}`` flag in the group's
+TCPStore strictly after its communicator joined, and the trainer polls those
+flags (:func:`wait_delta_wire_ready`) before its first publish.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import time
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+import torch
+import zmq
+
+from verl.utils.distributed import stateless_init_process_group
+from verl.utils.net_utils import is_valid_ipv6_address
+
+# A manifest is normally seconds behind its sender; a silent gap beyond this
+# means the sender stalled or died mid-session, so fail loud -- the session's
+# fail-fast abort then wakes the rest of the group instead of hanging it.
+MANIFEST_RECV_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300.0
+
+# vLLM startup + model load on the rollout side can take many minutes; the
+# sender waits at most this long for every receiver's wire-ready flag before
+# publishing the first manifest.
+WIRE_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1800.0
+
+
+def connect_delta_manifest_sub(zmq_ip: str, zmq_port: int, topic: str = "bucket_metadata") -> zmq.Socket:
+    """Subscribe to the trainer's flush-manifest PUB socket."""
+    context = zmq.Context()
+    sub = context.socket(zmq.SUB)
+    if is_valid_ipv6_address(zmq_ip):
+        sub.setsockopt(zmq.IPV6, 1)
+        sub.connect(f"tcp://[{zmq_ip}]:{zmq_port}")
+    else:
+        sub.connect(f"tcp://{zmq_ip}:{zmq_port}")
+    sub.setsockopt_string(zmq.SUBSCRIBE, topic)
+    return sub
+
+
+def build_delta_hccl_communicator(dist_ip: str, dist_port: int, group_rank: int, world_size: int, device):
+    """Join the trainer's PyHccl broadcast group at ``group_rank``."""
+    comm = stateless_init_process_group(dist_ip, dist_port, group_rank, world_size, device)
+    if group_rank > 0:
+        # Raised strictly after joining so the sender's pre-publish poll proves
+        # the SUB's SUBSCRIBE message already reached the PUB socket -- a
+        # process-level flag is the only sound receipt (zmq connect is async).
+        comm.group.store.add(f"delta_wire_ready/{group_rank}", 1)
+    return comm
+
+
+def wait_delta_wire_ready(store, num_receivers: int, timeout: float = WIRE_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) -> None:
+    """Block until group ranks ``1..num_receivers`` raised ``delta_wire_ready``.
+
+    ``store.add(key, 0)`` reads the counter without blocking, so a missing
+    receiver stays visible (and nameable in the TimeoutError) instead of
+    turning into a KeyError.
+    """
+    t0 = time.monotonic()
+    missing = list(range(1, num_receivers + 1))
+    while missing:
+        if time.monotonic() - t0 > timeout:
+            raise TimeoutError(
+                f"delta wire handshake timed out after {timeout:.0f}s: no wire-ready flag from group ranks {missing}"
+            )
+        missing = [r for r in missing if store.add(f"delta_wire_ready/{r}", 0) < 1]
+        if missing:
+            time.sleep(0.25)
+
+
+def pump_hccl_delta_session(
+    sub: zmq.Socket,
+    comm,
+    device,
+    on_flush: Callable[[list[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]], None],
+    group_rank: int | None = None,
+) -> str:
+    """Pull one delta session (manifests + broadcast payloads) and hand each
+    flush to ``on_flush(named_tensors)``.
+
+    Returns the session's wire encoding (``"dense"`` | ``"indices"``); a
+    terminal-only session (steady sync with zero changes) returns
+    ``"indices"`` with zero ``on_flush`` calls. The device synchronize after
+    each flush's broadcasts mirrors the sender: PyHccl enqueues on the current
+    stream, so the received buffers must not be read before completion. A
+    manifest gap beyond ``MANIFEST_RECV_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`` raises instead of
+    hanging: the sender stalled or died without destroying the group.
+    """
+    rank_tag = "?" if group_rank is None else str(group_rank)
+    synchronize = getattr(torch, device.type).synchronize
+    encoding = "indices"
+    while True:
+        if sub.poll(int(MANIFEST_RECV_TIMEOUT_SECONDS * 1000)) == 0:
+            raise TimeoutError(
+                f"delta-hccl pump rank={rank_tag}: no manifest within "
+                f"{MANIFEST_RECV_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:.0f}s; sender stalled mid-session or exited without destroying "
+                "the group"
+            )
+        sub.recv_string()
+        meta = sub.recv_pyobj()
+        if meta.get("terminal_empty"):
+            break
+        encoding = meta.get("encoding", "indices")
+        dense = encoding == "dense"
+        val_dtype = getattr(torch, meta["val_dtype"])
+        elem = torch.empty(0, dtype=val_dtype).element_size()
+        val_u8 = torch.empty(meta["val_numel"] * elem, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
+        if dense:
+            pos = None
+            comm.broadcast(val_u8, src=0)
+        else:
+            pos = torch.empty(meta["pos_numel"], dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
+            comm.broadcast(pos, src=0)
+            comm.broadcast(val_u8, src=0)
+        synchronize()
+        val = val_u8.view(val_dtype)
+        spec_bytes = json.dumps(meta["spec"]).encode()
+        spec_t = torch.frombuffer(bytearray(spec_bytes), dtype=torch.uint8).to(device)
+        named = [("__delta_spec__", spec_t), ("__values__", val)]
+        if pos is not None:
+            named.insert(1, ("__positions__", pos))
+        on_flush(named)
+        del pos, val_u8, val, spec_t
+        if meta["is_last"]:
+            break
+    return encoding

**Strengthen the wire checksum: the XOR-of-bytes fold carries only ~9 bits and ignores order.**

`_xor_tree` reduces each argument to the XOR of all its bytes, so the result is one value in `0..255`. `checksum` then combines `p` (8 bits) with `v << 1` (9 bits). A random corruption therefore passes verification with probability about 1/256.

The fold also does not depend on order. These failures all produce a matching checksum:
- Bytes or elements that are swapped or reordered inside a buffer.
- A shifted or misaligned receive buffer that contains the same byte multiset.
- Two corruptions of the same bit pattern, which cancel.

This change replaces `torch.hash_tensor` in the shared `encode.py`. The checksum is therefore weaker on the NCCL/CUDA path too, although the PR says CUDA behavior is unchanged. The HCCL engine comments say a missed manifest still fails loud by "per-flush checksum", and `decode_delta_wire` raises only on a checksum mismatch. A corrupted flush is then applied to rollout weights without any error.

A second cost: the first fold round allocates a temporary of half the flush size. For a 3072 MB bucket, that is about 1.5 GB on each receiver NPU.

Fold over 64-bit words so the result has 64 bits of entropy, and rotate the values term so the two inputs do not overlap. To also detect reordering, add a position-dependent term, for example a wraparound sum of `word * (index + 1)` computed in bounded chunks. Chunking also bounds the transient memory.

def _xor_tree(t: torch.Tensor) -> int:
    """Device-side XOR fold of a tensor's raw bytes (log2(n) rounds, one D2H).

    Replaces ``torch.hash_tensor`` (PyTorch >= 2.9, CPU/CUDA kernels only -- no
    NPU kernel, and its torch_npu CPU fallback costs a full D2H per call). The
    fold is out-of-place, so the argument's storage is never mutated, and it is
    a pure function of the bytes, so sender and receiver agree on any device.
    """
    if t.numel() == 0:
        return 0
    b = t.contiguous().reshape(-1).view(torch.uint8)
    n8 = b.numel() // 8 * 8
    tail = 0
    for i, x in enumerate(b[n8:].tolist()):  # < 8 bytes, host side
        tail ^= x << (8 * i)
    if n8 == 0:
        return tail
    v = b[:n8].view(torch.int64)
    # Halving XOR fold; an odd middle element carries to the next round.
    while v.numel() > 1:
        n = v.numel()
        half = n // 2
        if n % 2 == 0:
            v = v[:half] ^ v[half:]
        else:
            v = torch.cat((v[:half] ^ v[half + 1 :], v[half : half + 1]))
    return (int(v.item()) & ((1 << 64) - 1)) ^ tail

    XOR tree over each argument's bytes (device-side, one ``.item()`` sync per
    argument); the same function runs on both ends, so the value is stable
    across dtypes and devices.
    """
    p = _xor_tree(positions)
    v = _xor_tree(values)
    mask = (1 << 64) - 1
    v_rot = ((v << 1) | (v >> 63)) & mask
    return (p ^ v_rot) & mask

Addressed (folded into the HCCL-engine commit): the fold is now 64-bit and order-sensitive. Each little-endian int64 word is first mixed with its position (`w + K*(index+1)`, K odd, wraparound int64 == mod 2**64) and then XOR-folded, so any single changed word always changes the digest, and swapping two different words swaps their mixed values (the odd multiplier keeps position terms distinct), which the fold reports unless the XORs coincide (~2^-64). +## Ascend NPU (HCCL transport)
+
+The same ``delta_sharded`` backend ships an HCCL transport for Ascend NPU
+hosts. The checkpoint engine, wire schema, seed/steady state machine and flush
+manifests are shared with the NCCL variant — only the transport and the
+rollout-side receiver differ. No extra configuration: on NPU hosts the
+registry auto-selects the HCCL engine for the ``delta_sharded`` name (the NCCL
+delta module fails to import there — it needs cupy), and on CUDA hosts the
+NCCL engine keeps the name. Likewise the vLLM weight-transfer backend defaults
+to ``verl_delta_hccl`` on NPU and ``verl_delta_ipc`` elsewhere, so the same
+``backend=delta_sharded`` config drives both platforms.
+
+### How the transport differs
+
+- **Direct broadcast into the vLLM workers**: CUDA IPC
+  does not exist on NPU, so flushes are not forwarded through the rollout
+  adapter. Instead the trainer's rank 0 broadcasts each flush (positions +
+  values) into a **PyHccl broadcast group whose members are the vLLM worker
+  processes themselves** — one manifest subscription plus two broadcasts per
+  flush, no payload forwarding hop, no IPC handle negotiation. Group ranks:
+  trainer rank 0 at slot 0, rollout workers 1..N (replica-major /
+  tp-minor).
+- **Manifests over zmq PUB/SUB**: every flush is preceded by a manifest
+  published on a zmq PUB socket (topic ``bucket_metadata``). Receivers connect
+  their SUB *before* joining the broadcast group and raise a per-rank
+  ``delta_wire_ready`` flag in the group's TCPStore after joining; the trainer
+  polls those flags before publishing the first manifest. The flags are
+  required because ``zmq.Socket.connect()`` is asynchronous — a "connected"
+  SUB can still miss the first published manifest (a zmq PUB socket drops
+  messages published before any subscriber connected), and zmq offers no
+  subscription acknowledgment — the process-level wire-ready flag is the only
+  ordering signal available.
+- **Persistent group**: HCCL group setup is expensive, so the communicator is
+  built once at the first sync and kept across rounds (the vLLM worker
+  engines cache theirs too). ``rebuild_group=True`` raises
+  ``NotImplementedError``. A failed session destroys the communicator from
+  whichever side failed, so the whole group fails fast instead of hanging in
+  the next collective — a full job restart is required.

+  XOR tree rather than ``torch.hash_tensor`` (whose kernels are CPU/CUDA

Valid catch — confirmed end-to-end: with `torch_npu` installed but no NPU device, the import-only check lets `delta_hccl_checkpoint_engine` import (PyHccl is lazy, so nothing fails at import), silently take over the `"delta_sharded"` registration (`_registry[backend] = cls`, last-wins), reject an explicit CUDA-IPC config, and then crash in `torch.npu.current_device()` at construction.

Fixed by switching our three call sites to the full `is_torch_npu_available()` check (both platform-selection sites in `vllm_async_server.py`, plus the `DeltaHCCLCheckpointEngine` import guard), squashed into the commits that introduced them and force-pushed. No new import-time risk: `verl/utils/device.py` already runs the full check at module import (`is_npu_available = is_torch_npu_available()`).

We deliberately left the fourth site you suggested — the guard in `hccl_checkpoint_engine.py` — unchanged: that file is outside this PR's scope, and the same misconfiguration already misroutes upstream today (we reproduced the dense HCCL engine taking over the `"nccl"` name on such a host; `apply_npu_vllm_patches()` and `_resolve_sleep_level()` also key off `check_device=False`). That class of `check_device=False` platform decisions looks like a separate pre-existing issue worth its own ticket — happy to file one.

**Use a logical right shift for the avalanche step.** `v >> 31` is an arithmetic shift on `torch.int64`. The high bit of `v ^ (v >> 31)` is always zero, so a value and its bitwise complement produce the same avalanche input. The odd multiplication cannot restore that lost bit. This leaves deterministic single-word corruption collisions. For a word at 1-based position `p`, the values `w` and `(-1 - w - 2 * K * p) mod 2**64`, where `K = 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15`, produce complementary positioned words and the same digest. The current regression test does not cover this construction.

```diff +_LOW33_MASK = (1 << 33) - 1 # turns the arithmetic >> 31 into a logical shift _AVALANCHE_MIX = -0x00AE502812AA7333 ... - avalanched (``(v ^ v >> 31) * _AVALANCHE_MIX``; both steps bijective, see - the constant) before a halving XOR fold + avalanched (``(v ^ ((v >> 31) & _LOW33_MASK)) * _AVALANCHE_MIX``; the + logical shift makes both steps bijective) before a halving XOR fold ... - v = (v ^ (v >> 31)) * _AVALANCHE_MIX + v = (v ^ ((v >> 31) & _LOW33_MASK)) * _AVALANCHE_MIX ``` Update the reference helper to use the logical shift `u >> 31`, and add a regression for the same-position collision construction.

Follow-up to our earlier reply: the 64-bit order-sensitive XOR fold described there still admitted crafted swap collisions under adversarial analysis (two-bit word differences that stay position-invariant through the fold), so the current head (`a60e2045`) strengthens the wire digest to a 128-bit dual-stream design:

- Each little-endian int64 word is mixed with its position (odd multiplier, wraparound int64 == mod 2**64) and avalanched with masked (logical) xor-shift-multiply stages using the murmur3 fmix64 constants.
- The same mixed words feed two independent folds: a halving XOR tree and a mod-2**64 integer sum, combined as `(s_sum << 64) | s_xor`.
- Every mixing stage is bijective, so any single changed word always changes the digest — the original ~9-bit, order-blind fold concern no longer applies to either stream.
- A word swap collides only if the pair's mixed XOR-difference AND arithmetic difference are both constant across the swapped positions. Exhaustive family scans (structured pair universes, toggle neighborhoods over random seeds, and ~1M random-pair scans — 1.2M+ configurations in total) found zero joint families; every single-fold family found so far is non-constant in the other fold and is pinned as a regression: `test_bit63_word_pair_swap_is_detected`, `test_topbit_toggle_pair_swaps_are_detected`, `test_two_bit_shift_response_pair_swaps_are_detected`, `test_complementary_word_corruption_is_detected`.
- Integer addition is associative, so the sum fold is independent of reduction order and device; the same function runs on both ends.
- Unstructured collisions are ~2**-128, and any mismatch fails loud before the payload is applied.

Full guarantee notes live in the `_wire_digest` docstring (`verl/checkpoint_engine/delta_sync/encode.py`).

@HaoWang113 The supplied implementation addresses the original bytewise-width and order-blind-fold concerns. The bijective word mixing preserves detection of a single changed full word. The chunked processing also bounds the fold’s temporary allocations. One guarantee still needs correction: **the XOR and sum folds are not independent**.
